title: Universal Life Insurance Premium Processing Standard
content:
## 1. Flexible premiums

Premiums on Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance are flexible. The planned premium is a billing amount, not an obligation, and a planned premium change takes effect with the next billing. A planned-premium EFT draft day must be from day 1 to the tier's latest EFT draft day.

## 2. When a premium is accepted

A premium is accepted only while the policy status is applied, in force or in the grace period. The status is read from the policy record, not from the payer's account of it. An unscheduled payment must be at least the tier's smallest unscheduled premium.

## 3. Premium load and crediting

The premium load is the tier's load percentage up to target of the part of the premiums received in the policy year up to the target premium, plus the tier's excess load percentage of the part above it, rounded to the cent. The rest of the payment, the net premium, is credited to the account value on the date received and allocated according to the policy's indexed allocation percentage. The premiums of the policy year are those received since the latest policy anniversary on or before the payment, before the payment being loaded.

A conversion credit from an Ashgrove term conversion is credited as premium with no load.

*Worked figure (hypothetical).* An Ashgrove Protection UL (6% up to target, 3% above) has a target premium of $3000.00 and has received $2500.00 in the current policy year. A payment of $1000.00 falls $500.00 within the target and $500.00 above it: the load is 6% of $500.00, $30.00, plus 3% of $500.00, $15.00, a load of $45.00, and $955.00 is credited.

## 4. Guideline premium refund provision — no longer in force

The provision that a payment which would make premiums paid less withdrawals exceed the greater of the guideline single premium and the sum of guideline level premiums to date is refunded in the excess part within 60 days of receipt, unless it is needed to keep the policy in force, is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current basis for guideline excess refunds and is not applied.

## 5. Modified endowment contracts

A premium that would make the policy a modified endowment contract is accepted only with the owner's signed consent to modified endowment status on file; the consent is evidenced by a signed modified endowment consent request on the policy's service record.

The seven-pay test fails when the seven-pay premiums to date exceed the policy's seven-pay premium times the number of policy years begun within the first seven. The seven-pay premiums to date are the gross premiums received from the issue date to the earlier of the evaluation date and the seventh policy anniversary, less the premiums refunded in that period. When the test fails:

| Owner's signed consent on file | Result |
|---|---|
| No | The excess is refunded |
| Yes | The premium is accepted and the policy becomes a modified endowment contract permanently |

*Hypothetical case.* With a seven-pay premium of $10000.00, a policy in its third policy year may take $30000.00 of seven-pay premiums to date; a payment bringing them to $31000.00 fails the test by $1000.00.

superseded_clauses: A payment that would make premiums paid less withdrawals (ul_msr_cumulative_premiums) exceed the greater of the guideline single premium and the sum of guideline level premiums to date is refunded in the excess part within 60 days of receipt, unless it is needed to keep the policy in force.
